subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II scope, EU hosting locations, and dataflow (audit period)
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@fintrust.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fintrust.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — evidence scope + EU hosting questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the middle of our vendor risk review for Redwood as part of an upcoming procurement. A few specific asks from Legal and InfoSec:

- Copy of your latest SOC 2 Type II report and the exact audit period covered.
- A short bridge letter confirming whether the controls in the report remain in effect outside the report period and any limitations.
- Confirmation of where customer data can be hosted/processed for Redwood Hosted API versus Dedicated/Private deployments (we need explicit EU hosting guarantees for prod workloads).
- A dataflow diagram and confirmation whether telemetry/logs or aggregated metrics are transferred out of the EU. If so, what safeguards (SCCs, encryption, KMS region) are in place?

Also: are you able to confirm that the SOC 2 scope covers the control plane and the data plane for Dedicated customers in eu-west-1, or is the report limited to the control plane and US-hosted services?

We have a target decision date of 2026-11-20, so if you can get these artifacts and clarifications to us this week that would be very helpful.

Best,
Emma
Emma Lewis
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager, FinTrust Bank
emma.lewis@fintrust.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 13:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — evidence scope + EU hosting questions

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, full detail below and I attached a short summary pack and a dataflow diagram.

TL;DR:
- We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report for the period 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (attached summary + full report available under NDA).
- We can provide a bridge letter confirming controls remain in effect for up to 90 days post-report; for longer commitments we can provide a tailored letter after legal review.
- Hosting options: Hosted API (default) routes requests to our nearest region and may be processed outside the EU; Dedicated (reserved capacity) can be provisioned in eu-west-1 (AWS) or other EU regions on request; Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) remains fully within customer-managed boundaries.
- Telemetry & logs: aggregated operational metrics are collected for platform health and are pseudo-anonymized. For Dedicated & Private customers we can restrict log export to EU regions and limit telemetry scope — details in dataflow diagram and attachments. We use SCCs for outbound transfers and customer KMS is supported in EU regions.

Details and next steps:
1) SOC 2 report: the current Type II report covers our production control plane and hosted managed inference service controls as of the period above. It does not assert geographic residency guarantees — it reports controls around change management, access, monitoring, incident response, and vendor management. If you need the auditor to explicitly attest to Dedicated eu-west-1 instances being in scope, we can work with our auditor to provide a scoped assertion or a supplemental letter, but that requires confirmation of the deployment model and a short lead time.

2) Bridge letter: attached "bridge-letter-draft.pdf" — this is our standard wording confirming there have been no material control changes since the report period and describing the scope. If you need statements about SCCs and GDPR controls specifically for FinTrust, we will ask Legal to tailor the letter (approx. 3-5 business days).

3) Dataflow and telemetry: attached is a simplified dataflow (redwood-dataflow-eu-uk.png). In short: for Dedicated in eu-west-1, customer data and KV caches reside in that region. Audit logs and operational traces can be configured to remain in the same region. We do, by default, collect aggregated service telemetry that is stored in our control plane; for customers requiring strict residency we can enable EU-only telemetry. SCCs are in place for transfers; we support customer-managed KMS keys in EU regions.

4) Token/logging: our default Hosted API retains short-lived runtime logs for debugging (rotated and purged per our retention policy). We can provide a retention schedule and, for Dedicated, options to disable token-level logging to meet stricter requirements.

What we need from you to finalize artifacts:
- Confirmation which deployment model you plan to use in prod (Hosted vs Dedicated in eu-west-1 vs Private).
- Whether FinTrust requires explicit auditor attestation that Dedicated eu-west-1 instances were in scope in the last audit period (this affects timeline).

Next steps: Marissa / Rishi from our team will loop in procurement and legal on bridge-letter tailoring and NDA for the full report. If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute call with the InfoSec team tomorrow.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@fintrust.com>

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — evidence scope + EU hosting questions

Hi Olga — thanks, that helps a lot. A few clarifications from InfoSec and Legal after reviewing your summary: 

- We will be targeting Dedicated in eu-west-1 for production; please confirm whether the auditor included eu-west-1 Dedicated instances in the Type II period or whether this would require a supplemental attestation.
- On telemetry: can you confirm whether any personally-identifiable metadata (user IDs, email addresses) appear in the operational traces that are retained by the control plane by default? If yes, are those encrypted and where (region) are the keys held?
- Can you provide the specific SCC clause reference(s) or a short statement of which transfer mechanism you rely on (SCCs, UK Addendum, or adequacy)?

Separately, Legal asked whether the bridge letter template can explicitly state "no material changes affecting the effectiveness of the controls in scope" and include the auditor name and report date. Is that standard for you?

If you can confirm those three points and share the full report under NDA, we can move to procurement.

Thanks,
Emma

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@fintrust.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — evidence scope + EU hosting questions

Hi Emma — looping in procurement / legal tracking. Quick answers while Olga / security finalize wording: 

- Dedicated eu-west-1: our last Type II report did not include a customer-by-customer attestation of Dedicated provisioning in specific regions. The underlying controls for Dedicated are included (configuration management, segregation, monitoring), but if you require the auditor to confirm that your specific Dedicated instances in eu-west-1 were observed during the audit, that is a scoped attestation we can pursue. It will need a short engagement with the auditor (usually 1-2 weeks) plus access confirmation.

- Telemetry / PII: by default operational traces do not store customer PII fields. We can provide a sanitized example trace showing field-level redaction. Customer-managed KMS is available in eu-west-1; if you opt to use it, keys (and therefore decryption) are under your control and region-bound.

- Transfer mechanism: we rely on the EU SCCs (latest 2021 clauses) with the UK Addendum where applicable; we can provide the legal reference text and your counsel can request our DPA addendum.

Action items I will run:
1) Send NDA/secure link for full SOC 2 report.
2) Confirm with Olga whether we can add auditor name and exact language "no material changes affecting the effectiveness of the controls in scope" to the bridge letter (should be possible; legal will confirm).
3) If FinTrust wants the auditor to include a scoped attestation for your Dedicated instances in eu-west-1, tell us the planned deployment window and we will coordinate timelines.

I'll drop a calendar invite for a 30-min call Monday to finalize.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
